title: His marriage to Vivian Greenne, 1933
summary: He tells the comic story of marrying Vivian Greenne in Omaha on June 23, 1933, urged by Buddy Tate's wife Vi, with his mother visiting.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: I was married for 2 weeks and when the guys brought me home I said, "I'm married." They said, "You're crazy. You're not married." I said, "Yes, I am."
Where'd they bring you home to?
I was staying in one place and I told them to take me to another address, because my wife was waiting on me.

Omaha, Nebraska. Her father was a minister. I wasn't going to get married! Milt, I wouldn't have married the Queen of Sheba with diamonds on and everybody knew that I wasn't going to get married and when I had to go down to the Omaha World Herald and get some old newspapers and go down the street to the pool halls and everywhere to show the people that I got married. They just didn't believe it. I didn't believe it myself! My mother came all the way from Chicago to say, "I want to see the woman that's going to marry my son." And come to think of it, after my mother got there I didn't get a chance to see my wife because my mother was going out with my wife. I never saw her! They was going out together. Now you know who made me get married?

Vi. Like Vivian and like your wife's name. Vi. My mother and myself were staying in her home on 27th Street, in Omaha. Scotty the guitarist, Dr. Scott's son, who was a heck of a guitarist and a singer, was staying across the street. At that particular time Vi was married to Jimmy Jones—that was the trombone player that eventually came to New York and worked for Noble Sissel at the Diamond Horseshoe on bass. I don't know nothing about their personal

life but eventually they did get a divorce and you know Vi's married to Buddy now. But HINTON: Vi - oh, she was married to Jimmy Jones at one time. JONES: Vi told me to marry the one I married. I hadn't spoken to her in 6 months and I talked to her. I said, "Would you marry me?" because I wanted to get with this band.
